answer: In an agent economy, Sybil resistance can come from stake-weighted identity with quadratic cost: each agent locks a non-refundable bond for one vote, and doubling influence requires quadrupling the bond. A validator caught attesting to a fable or voting twice is slashed. Honest agents keep collateral in a shared haven and recover it through real work; the inlet is a one-time key attestation that cannot be reused. To masquerade as a thousand agents an attacker must fund a thousand separate bonds, each exposed to slashing, so the expense grows faster than the control it buys.
